channel.title: Clinical Research Chaos – open funding calls
channel.description: Open funding calls in clinical research, clinical engineering and rehabilitation, checked on the official text.

item.title: Identify and Evaluate Potential Risk Factors for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
item.description: CDC and ATSDR invite research proposals to evaluate risk factors for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis. Funding supports four areas: research on established environmental or genetic factors, exploratory research using innovative methods, risk in affected populations such as military veterans, and biological sample analysis from the Guamanian ALS cluster. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, state and local governments, tribal governments and organizations, school districts, and public housing authorities. Programme: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention - ERA. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: 1 Dec 2026. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363115

item.title: Advanced Rehabilitation Research Training (ARRT) Program - Community Living and Participation
item.description: This opportunity under the Advanced Rehabilitation Research Training (ARRT) Program aims to provide advanced multidisciplinary research training to individuals with doctorates or similar advanced degrees, including researchers with disabilities. Funded projects must focus on community living and participation outcomes for people with disabilities. A single grant with a 36-month project period will be awarded. Public, state-controlled, and private institutions of higher education are eligible to apply; foreign entities are excluded. Programme: Advanced Rehabilitation Research Training (ARRT) Program. Eligible countries: United States only. Deadline: 7 Dec 2026. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/363963

item.title: HEAL Initiative: Integrative Management of Chronic Pain and OUD for Whole Recovery (IMPOWR): Research Centers
item.description: This funding opportunity aims to renew the Integrative Management of chronic Pain and OUD for Whole Recovery (IMPOWR) research network, supporting individual research projects coordinated by a central center. The goal is to test improved approaches for individuals suffering from both chronic pain and opioid use disorder to enhance health system care delivery. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign institutions, higher education, non-profits, tribal governments, and other specified organizations. Programme: NIH HEAL Initiative. Eligible countries: Coming soon: published with the full call. Deadline: 26 Jan 2027. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/360048

item.title: NCMRR Early Career Research Award (R03 Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: The NCMRR Early Career Research Award supports rehabilitation scientists in establishing independent research careers by funding basic or clinical research projects. The aim is to collect preliminary data for a subsequent R01 application. Eligible applicant organizations include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, governments, and foreign organizations. Early-stage investigators who are no more than 8 years past their terminal degree may apply as lead investigators. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Must be an independent investigator, no more than 8 years beyond the date their terminal academic degree was awarded. Not a postdoctoral fellow at submission.. Next deadline: 16 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357206

item.title: Parkinson's Disease Therapeutics Pipeline Program
item.description: This funding initiative accelerates Parkinson’s disease therapy development by funding pre-clinical and clinical development of disease-modifying or symptomatic interventions, as well as biomarker tools. Funding ranges from $250,000 to upwards of $5M for 1 to 3 years. The call is open to industry, academic/industry partnerships, and academic-led projects in certain cases. Applications follow a two-stage process with rolling pre-proposals and full proposals submitted by invitation. Programme: Parkinson's Disease Therapeutics Pipeline Program. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Who can lead: Open to industry, academic/industry partnerships, and—in certain cases—academic-led projects.. Stage 1 deadline: 30 Oct 2026 (two-stage call). Official call: https://www.michaeljfox.org/grant/parkinsons-disease-therapeutics-pipeline-program

item.title: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research Grant Program (BFDN)
item.description: This funding program aims to support early career investigators whose Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and related neurodegenerative research projects have been disrupted by changes or challenges in U.S. federal research funding. It funds salary and direct costs for projects facing delays, termination, priority misalignment, or funding gaps. Principal investigators must be early-stage investigators under NIH guidelines or within 7 years of their ESI designation, and host institutions must provide cost-sharing. Programme: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research Grant Program (BFDN). Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Who can lead: All Principal Investigators must be an early-stage investigator under the NIH guidelines or within 7 years of their ESI designation.. Next deadline: 30 Oct 2026 (new applications). Official call: https://www.michaeljfox.org/grant/bridge-funding-disrupted-neurodegenerative-research-grant-program-bfdn-powering-next

item.title: Clinical trials for advancing innovative interventions for neurodegenerative diseases
item.description: This Horizon Europe call aims to support early-stage clinical trials evaluating the safety and efficacy of innovative, multi-disciplinary therapeutic interventions combined with complementary approaches for neurodegenerative diseases. Funded projects should improve patient quality of life, utilise health data according to FAIR principles, engage relevant stakeholders including patients, and leverage research infrastructures. Eligible applicants include international consortia composed of legal entities such as universities, clinical centres, and SMEs established in EU Member States or Associated Countries. Programme: Horizon Europe. Eligible countries: EU Member States and associated countries. Stage 1 deadline: 17 Feb 2027 (two-stage call). Official call: https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/portal/screen/opportunities/topic-details/HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-DISEASE-14-two-stage

item.title: DoW Parkinson's, Early Investigator Research Award
item.description: The Early Investigator Research Award supports early-career investigators in conducting innovative Parkinson's disease research. It offers two funding levels: Level 1 for fellows requiring a mentor, and Level 2 for early-career independent investigators requiring preliminary data. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign public, private, for-profit, and nonprofit organizations. Proposed research must address specific Parkinson's disease focus areas and benefit military and civilian populations. Clinical trials are not allowed. Programme: CDMRP – Parkinson’s Research Program (PRP). Eligible countries: Any country. Who can lead: Postdoctoral fellows, clinical fellows, or independent investigators within 10 years of advanced degree or residency training completion, or equivalent.. Deadline: 6 Nov 2026. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362866

item.title: DoW Parkinson’s, Investigator-Initiated Research Award
item.description: The Investigator-Initiated Research Award supports highly rigorous, multidisciplinary, high-impact research projects addressing Parkinson's disease across basic science to clinical trials. Funded research must target at least one specific FY26 Parkinson's Research Program focus area and require preliminary data. Independent investigators at all academic levels affiliated with eligible domestic or foreign organizations can apply, with total costs capped at $2 million over a maximum three-year performance period. Programme: CDMRP – Parkinson’s Research Program (PRP). Eligible countries: Any country. Who can lead: Independent investigators at all academic levels, or equivalent, affiliated with an eligible organization, regardless of ethnicity, nationality or citizenship s. Deadline: 6 Nov 2026. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362868

item.title: Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Translational Research Award
item.description: The fiscal year 2026 Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Translational Research Award supports translational research that will accelerate the movement of promising ideas in spinal cord injury research into clinical applications. The call funds preclinical evaluations, clinical studies, and pilot trials addressing acute injury intervention, secondary health effects, psychosocial well-being, or rehabilitation. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign, for-profit and nonprofit, public and private organizations. Proposals must name at least one spinal cord injury community partner. Programme: Defense Health Agency Spinal Cord Injury Research Program. Eligible countries: Any country. Who can lead: Independent investigators at all career levels can apply as Single PI. For Early-Career Partnership, at least one PI must be within 7 years of first faculty app. Stage 1 deadline: 12 Nov 2026 (two-stage call). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362222

item.title: DoW Spinal Cord Injury, Clinical Trial Award
item.description: The fiscal year 2026 Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Clinical Trial Award supports the rapid implementation of clinical trials to significantly impact the treatment or management of spinal cord injury. Funding is available for single or partnering principal investigators, requiring at least two spinal cord community partners. Extramural and intramural organizations worldwide, including foreign and domestic, for-profit and nonprofit, are eligible to apply. Programme: CDMRP – Spinal Cord Injury Research Program (SCIRP). Eligible countries: Any country. Who can lead: Independent investigators at all career levels. For the partnership option, at least one PI must be an early-career investigator as specified.. Deadline: 12 Nov 2026. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362224

item.title: DoW Spinal Cord Injury, Clinical Translation Research Award
item.description: The fiscal year 2026 Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Clinical Translation Research Award supports high-impact clinical research and clinical trials requiring preliminary studies to prepare for larger-scale implementation. The funding aims to accelerate the translation of interventions into clinical use and identify optimal diagnostic and treatment options. Eligible applicants include domestic and foreign organizations, and the call features an early-career partnership option and a requirement for community collaboration. Programme: CDMRP – Spinal Cord Injury Research Program (SCIRP). Eligible countries: Any country. Who can lead: Independent investigators at all career levels. For the Early-Career Partnership Option, at least one PI must be an early-career investigator.. Stage 1 deadline: 12 Nov 2026 (two-stage call). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362225

item.title: Engineering Biological and Biomedical Systems (EBBS)
item.description: The Engineering Biological and Biomedical Systems program expands our understanding of biological and physiological systems to improve human health. It supports fundamental engineering research combining mechanistic insights with experimental and computational techniques to develop platforms, devices, tissues, and processes. Eligible applicants include a wide range of entities as specified by the funding agency, focusing on foundational discoveries rather than clinical trials or commercialization. Programme: U.S. National Science Foundation. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/362062

item.title: Clinical Trials Addressing Unmet Needs of Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases (R01)
item.description: This funding opportunity aims to support clinical trials evaluating the efficacy and safety of products to address unmet medical needs in rare neurodegenerative diseases for both children and adults. Funded through the R01 mechanism by the Food and Drug Administration, the initiative seeks to increase approved treatments and have a broad, positive impact on rare disease drug development. Eligible applicants include a wide variety of organizational types such as educational institutions, nonprofits, and for-profit entities. Programme: Food and Drug Administration. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356054

item.title: Studies Addressing Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases including ALS
item.description: This funding opportunity supports studies that advance medical product development of interventions intended to prevent, diagnose, mitigate, treat, or cure ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases in adults and children. The initiative aims to address critical knowledge gaps, make a significant impact on rare neurodegenerative diseases, and inform current or future product development. Various entity types, including governments, educational institutions, nonprofits, and for-profit organizations, are eligible to apply. Programme: Food and Drug Administration. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356046

item.title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) Intermediate Patient Population Expanded Access
item.description: This funding opportunity solicits applications to conduct scientific research utilizing data from expanded access for investigational drugs or biological products. The research targets intermediate size populations of patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis who are ineligible for ongoing clinical trials. Eligible applicants are clinical trial sites participating in specific phase 2/3 or phase 3 efficacy clinical trials supported by an FDA-designated small business sponsor. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Eligible applicants must be clinical trial sites that participate in a phase 2/3 or phase 3 efficacy clinical trial supported by an FDA-designated small busines. Deadline: 10 Nov 2026. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/360400

item.title: Promotion of Doctoral Studies Scholarships
item.description: The Foundation for Physical Therapy Research offers scholarships supporting licensed physical therapists and physical therapist assistants who are APTA members and pursuing an academic doctoral degree with the intent to pursue a research career in physical therapy. The call provides funding for two phases: pre-candidates receive annual awards of $7,500 for coursework, while doctoral candidates receive $15,000 annually for the candidacy phase. Programme: Promotion of Doctoral Studies Scholarships. Eligible countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call. Who can lead: Licensed physical therapists and physical therapist assistants who are APTA members pursuing a PhD, EdD, DSc, or other academic doctoral degrees.. Deadline: 20 Jan 2027. Official call: https://foundation4pt.org/foundation-funding-opportunities/scholarships/

item.title: NIA Academic Leadership Career Award (K07 Independent Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
item.description: The National Institute on Aging offers support for established investigators to enhance aging and Alzheimer's Disease or related dementias research and educational capacity within their academic institution. The award funds research and educational infrastructure, mentorship, and career development activities such as courses, pilot funding, and travel awards. Applicants must be US-based established investigators holding a doctoral degree and a named PD/PI role on an active R01 or equivalent NIA grant. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Next deadline: 12 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/357000

item.title: Development of Biomarkers or Composite Biomarkers for Neurological and Neuromuscular Disorders (R61/R33 - Clinical Trial Optional)
item.description: This NIH funding opportunity promotes the discovery and development of candidate biomarkers or composite biomarkers for neurological and neuromuscular disorders. The phased R61/R33 mechanism supports initial proof-of-concept studies and preliminary clinical validation to ensure biomarkers are fit for use in clinical trials or clinical practice. Eligible applicant organizations include domestic U.S. higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit entities, and government bodies. Foreign entities are not eligible to apply. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Any individual(s) with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to carry out the proposed research as the Program Director(s)/Principal Investigator(s).. Next deadline: 22 Feb 2027 (new applications). Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/356874

item.title: Grants for Early Medical/Surgical Specialists' Transition to Aging Research (GEMSSTAR)
item.description: The GEMSSTAR program aims to support early-career clinician-scientists in medical or surgical specialties to launch research careers focused on aging or geriatrics. It funds transdisciplinary pilot projects and professional development plans within supportive research environments. Only U.S.-based organizations are eligible to apply, as foreign organizations and foreign subawards are strictly excluded from this funding opportunity. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: United States only (foreign organisations not eligible). Who can lead: Early-career clinician-scientists trained in medical or surgical specialties.. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/359940

item.title: NINDS Efficacy and Exploratory Clinical Trials (UG3/UH3 - Clinical Trial Required)
item.description: This funding opportunity invites investigator-initiated clinical trials addressing neurological diseases and disorders within the mission of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS). Supported projects include early- and middle-phase exploratory clinical trials as well as later-phase confirmatory Phase 3 or comparative effectiveness trials involving small molecules, biologics, devices, and behavioral or rehabilitation therapies across the lifespan. Various domestic and foreign organizational types are eligible to apply. Programme: NIH – US National Institutes of Health. Eligible countries: Any country (non-US organisations eligible). Who can lead: Refer to Section III. Eligibility Information in the NOFO for additional information on eligibility.. Deadline: see the official call. Official call: https://www.grants.gov/search-results-detail/360404
